name: C++ Object-Oriented & Systems Track
description: Master modern C++17/C++20 object-oriented design, constructors/destructors, inheritance, virtual polymorphism, generic Templates, Standard Template Library (STL), and Smart Pointers.
whatYouLearn: Master C++ Class architecture, encapsulation, and initializer lists
Implement Inheritance, virtual functions, and runtime Polymorphism
Write generic functions and classes using C++ Templates
Utilize Standard Template Library containers (std::vector, std::map, std::unordered_map)
Prevent memory leaks using RAII and Smart Pointers (std::unique_ptr, std::shared_ptr)
Build a production Game Engine Logic Core

exercises.title: Classes, Constructors & Initializer Lists
exercises.description: Build C++ classes with constructors, member initializer lists, and getter/setter methods.
exercises.theory: C++ classes group data and methods under access specifiers (public, private, protected). Member initializer lists initialize fields before constructor execution.
exercises.objective: Build a Player class with constructor initializer list.
requirements: Declare private fields name, level, health
Use constructor member initializer list syntax : name(n), level(l), health(h)
hints: const after method signature promises method will not modify object state
exercises.codeExample: class Car { int speed; public: Car(s) : speed(s) {} };

exercises.title: Destructors & RAII Memory Management
exercises.description: Implement destructors (~ClassName) following RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization).
exercises.theory: Destructors (~ClassName) execute automatically when objects go out of scope, releasing acquired heap resources automatically (RAII idiom).
exercises.objective: Build a BufferResource class with custom destructor cleanup.
requirements: Allocate heap memory in constructor using new int[size]
Deallocate heap memory in destructor using delete[] buffer
Demonstrate automatic destructor execution upon scope exit
hints: Always match new[] with delete[] and single new with single delete
exercises.codeExample: class Res { int *p; public: Res() { p = new int; } ~Res() { delete p; } };

exercises.title: Copy Constructors & Deep Copying
exercises.description: Prevent double-free bugs by writing custom copy constructors performing deep memory copying.
exercises.theory: Default copy constructors perform shallow member-wise copies. Classes managing dynamic raw pointers require custom deep copy constructors.
exercises.objective: Write a deep copy constructor for dynamic array class.
requirements: Write copy constructor syntax ClassName(const ClassName& other)
Allocate new memory array and copy individual elements
hints: Passing reference parameter const ClassName& avoids recursive copy constructor calls
exercises.codeExample: Obj(const Obj& other) { data = new int(*other.data); }

exercises.title: Inheritance & Access Specifiers (public, protected)
exercises.description: Extend base classes using public inheritance and protected member variables.
exercises.theory: Subclasses inherit base class properties. protected members are accessible inside derived subclasses but hidden from public scope.
exercises.objective: Build Entity base class and Character subclass.
requirements: Create base Entity class with protected fields
Inherit publicly using class Character : public Entity
Call base constructor Entity(n, x, y) in subclass initializer list
hints: protected members allow child classes direct field access
exercises.codeExample: class Child : public Parent { public: Child() : Parent() {} };

exercises.title: Virtual Functions & Polymorphism (virtual, override)
exercises.description: Achieve dynamic runtime polymorphism using virtual methods and virtual destructors.
exercises.theory: Declaring base methods with virtual enables dynamic dispatch. Subclasses override virtual methods. Always make base destructors virtual.
exercises.objective: Build polymorphic Shape base class and Circle / Rectangle subclasses.
requirements: Declare virtual void draw() const in base Shape class
Use override keyword in Circle subclass
hints: override keyword ensures compiler verifies function signature matches base virtual method exactly
exercises.codeExample: virtual void render() override;

exercises.title: Pure Virtual Functions & Abstract Classes
exercises.description: Create abstract interface classes containing pure virtual functions (= 0).
exercises.theory: A function marked with = 0 is a pure virtual function. Classes containing pure virtual functions are abstract and cannot be directly instantiated.
exercises.objective: Build abstract IRenderable interface.
requirements: Declare virtual void render() = 0; pure virtual function
Implement render() in Button derived class
hints: Pure virtual functions define pure contract interfaces that subclasses MUST implement
exercises.codeExample: virtual void log() = 0;

exercises.title: Operator Overloading
exercises.description: Overload arithmetic (+, -) and stream insertion (<<) operators.
exercises.theory: Operator overloading permits custom class objects to operate using native operators (+, -, ==, <<).
exercises.objective: Overload + operator and << stream operator for a Vector2D class.
requirements: Overload Vector2D operator+(const Vector2D& other) const
Overload friend std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream&, const Vector2D&)
hints: friend functions allow non-member stream operators access to private class members
exercises.codeExample: Vector2D operator+(const Vector2D& v) const { return Vector2D(x+v.x, y+v.y); }

exercises.title: Function & Class Templates (template <typename T>)
exercises.description: Write generic functions and classes using C++ Templates.
exercises.theory: Templates enable generic programming. The compiler generates specialized code for each concrete type passed to template parameters.
exercises.objective: Build generic template function maxVal<T>() and class Box<T>.
requirements: Write template <typename T> T getMax(T a, T b)
hints: template <typename T> must precede every template function or class definition
exercises.codeExample: template <typename T> T add(T a, T b) { return a + b; }

exercises.title: STL std::vector & Iterators
exercises.description: Manipulate dynamic arrays using std::vector and STL iterators.
exercises.theory: std::vector is a dynamic array template from the Standard Template Library. Traverse vectors using iterator loops or range-based for loops.
exercises.objective: Manipulate std::vector elements and iterate using range-based for loop.
requirements: Iterate using range-based for loop for (const auto& num : numbers)
hints: std::sort sorts elements in ascending order in O(N log N) time
exercises.codeExample: std::vector<int> vec; vec.push_back(1);

exercises.title: STL Key-Value Maps (std::map & std::unordered_map)
exercises.description: Store and retrieve key-value pairs using std::map and std::unordered_map.
exercises.theory: std::map stores ordered key-value pairs using Red-Black Trees O(log N). std::unordered_map uses Hash Tables for average O(1) lookups.
exercises.objective: Store and query student grades using std::unordered_map.
hints: find() returns map.end() iterator if key is absent
exercises.codeExample: std::unordered_map<std::string, int> map; map["a"] = 1;

exercises.title: Smart Pointers: std::unique_ptr
exercises.description: Manage exclusive-ownership dynamic memory safely using std::unique_ptr.
exercises.theory: std::unique_ptr guarantees exclusive ownership of dynamic heap memory, preventing memory leaks by auto-deleting when unique_ptr leaves scope.
exercises.objective: Allocate objects with std::make_unique<T>() and transfer ownership using std::move().
hints: std::unique_ptr cannot be copied, only moved using std::move()
exercises.codeExample: auto ptr = std::make_unique<int>(42);

exercises.title: Smart Pointers: std::shared_ptr & std::weak_ptr
exercises.description: Manage shared reference-counted memory using std::shared_ptr and break cyclic references with std::weak_ptr.
exercises.theory: std::shared_ptr shares ownership across multiple owners using reference counting. std::weak_ptr provides a non-owning observer pointer to break retain cycles.
exercises.objective: Demonstrate reference count tracking with std::shared_ptr.
requirements: Copy shared pointer to increment reference count
hints: Memory is freed only when the internal reference count drops to 0
exercises.codeExample: auto p1 = std::make_shared<int>(10); auto p2 = p1;

exercises.title: Lambda Expressions ([capture](params) -> ret)
exercises.description: Write inline C++ lambda functions with value and reference capture clauses.
exercises.theory: Lambdas are anonymous inline functions. Capture clauses [=], [&], [var] control access to outer variables.
exercises.objective: Write C++ lambda expressions with capture clauses for std::count_if.
requirements: Write lambda with capture [threshold](int score) -> bool
hints: [=] captures all outer variables by value; [&] captures by reference
exercises.codeExample: auto add = [](int a, int b) { return a + b; };

exercises.title: Move Semantics & Rvalue References (&&)
exercises.description: Eliminate expensive deep copies using rvalue references (&&) and move constructors.
exercises.theory: Move semantics transfer ownership of resources from temporary rvalues without allocating new heap memory blocks.
exercises.objective: Implement a move constructor ClassName(ClassName&& other) noexcept.
requirements: Write move constructor Buffer(Buffer&& other) noexcept
Transfer pointer ownership and set other.data = nullptr
hints: Setting source pointer to nullptr in move constructor prevents destructor double-free errors
exercises.codeExample: Buffer(Buffer&& o) noexcept : data(o.data) { o.data = nullptr; }

exercises.title: C++ Exception Handling (try, catch, throw)
exercises.description: Throw custom exception objects and catch exception hierarchies.
exercises.theory: C++ exception handling uses try, catch, and throw. Standard exceptions inherit from std::exception.
exercises.objective: Throw std::runtime_error and catch exception reference.
requirements: Catch const std::runtime_error& and print e.what()
hints: e.what() returns the error message string passed to the exception constructor
exercises.codeExample: try { throw std::runtime_error("err"); } catch (const std::exception& e) {}

exercises.title: Type Casting (static_cast, dynamic_cast)
exercises.description: Perform compile-time static_cast and runtime polymorphic dynamic_cast.
exercises.theory: static_cast converts compatible types at compile time. dynamic_cast safely downcasts polymorphic base class pointers at runtime.
exercises.objective: Perform safe dynamic_cast downcasting on polymorphic class pointers.
requirements: Check derivedPtr != nullptr guard before invoking child methods
hints: dynamic_cast returns nullptr if the underlying object is NOT an instance of target derived class
exercises.codeExample: Derived* d = dynamic_cast<Derived*>(b);

exercises.title: Enum Classes (enum class)
exercises.description: Group scoped, strongly-typed constants using enum class.
exercises.theory: enum class defines strongly-typed, scoped enumerations that do not implicitly convert to integers or leak names into enclosing scope.
exercises.objective: Declare an enum class State and use in switch statements.
requirements: Access members using scope resolution operator GameState::Playing
hints: enum class prevents name collisions by keeping enum values scoped inside the enum name
exercises.codeExample: enum class Color { Red, Blue }; Color c = Color::Red;

exercises.title: Namespaces & Scope Resolution (namespace, ::)
exercises.description: Prevent global naming collisions using custom namespaces.
exercises.theory: Namespaces partition code identifiers into distinct named logical scopes.
exercises.objective: Declare custom namespace ByteCode and invoke nested functions.
requirements: Invoke using scope resolution operator ByteCode::Engine::initialize()
hints: Avoid writing using namespace std; in header files to prevent scope pollution
exercises.codeExample: namespace App { void run() {} } App::run();

exercises.title: Chrono Library & Execution Benchmarking (std::chrono)
exercises.description: Measure precise code execution duration using <chrono> high-resolution clocks.
exercises.theory: std::chrono::high_resolution_clock measures high-precision time intervals for code performance benchmarking.
exercises.objective: Measure execution time of a computation loop using std::chrono.
requirements: Capture start and end timestamps with std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now()
Calculate duration in milliseconds with elapsed.count()
hints: duration<double, std::milli> outputs elapsed time formatted as floating point milliseconds
exercises.codeExample: auto t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();

exercises.title: Capstone Project: Object-Oriented Game Logic Engine Core
exercises.description: Engineered a production-grade Game Engine Logic Core featuring Polymorphic Game Objects, Smart Pointers (std::unique_ptr), Templates, and STL Containers.
exercises.theory: This capstone project synthesizes modern C++17 architecture: Abstract interface classes, dynamic polymorphism, smart pointer ownership (std::unique_ptr), std::vector container management, and RAII resource safety.
exercises.objective: Construct a complete Game Engine Core system.
requirements: Define abstract GameObject interface with pure virtual update/render methods
hints: std::unique_ptr enforces clean automatic destruction of game objects without memory leaks
exercises.codeExample: std::vector<std::unique_ptr<GameObject>> objects;

references.title: C++ Reference (ISO/IEC 14882)
references.description: Comprehensive reference manual for C++ language syntax, STL algorithms, and memory models
